hinglish.phrase: Zyada kisne beche—Event A ya Event B—and kaunsa place-value group faisla karta hai?
hinglish.why: Stray English "and" left in the Hinglish sentence (should be "aur"). Also prompt_hi never says which number belongs to Event A and which to Event B (prompt_en does: A = 4,09,80,000, B = 4,10,02,000); only the listing order implies it.

other_notes: All 188 items solved blind; every stored key (answer, worked-example steps/faded, MCQ flagged option) matches my answer in substance. No acceptable form found that is an outright wrong answer.

pl-c6-maths-e01: wording is loose ("1, 3, 6, 10, 15 seats in successive triangular rows" - these are triangular numbers, not row sizes of one triangle), but as a sequence the next term 21 is unambiguous; key 21 is right.

pl-c7-maths-e07: prompt_en asks for the "value of the digit 6" in 24.68, prompt_hi asks for its "place value"; in NCERT usage both give 0.6, so the key holds, but the two prompts are not the same wording.

Placement keys with a fraction answer and no acceptable list: pl-c6-maths-l01 (3/4 m; 0.75 is equally correct), pl-c6-maths-m12 (3/4 litre; 0.75), pl-c6-maths-l02 (1 3/4; question asks mixed fraction so fine), pl-c7-maths-m08 (1/2 litre; 0.5). Only pl-c6-maths-l05 lists decimal/mixed alternatives. Whether this matters depends on whether the grader normalises equivalent numeric forms.

Several teaching-kit acceptable lists contain half-answers to two-part questions (e.g. c6-maths-ch04-t03-i10 accepts "March" alone or "4 GB" alone; c6-maths-ch07-t01-i07 accepts "more than half" alone; c7-maths-ch03-t02-i05 accepts "smaller" alone). They are true but incomplete, not wrong.
c7-maths-ch02-t01-i12 ("Write an expression for 12 less than 40") accepts "28", which is the value rather than an expression; not a wrong number.

c7-maths-ch03-t03-rl-h3: acceptable list contains the descriptive string "any decimal strictly greater than 2.307 and less than 2.308", which is a rule, not a matchable answer form; valid answers such as 2.30705 are covered only if the grader applies that rule.
Correction to my own phase-1 note on c6-maths-ch06-t01-i10: the side order 6, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4 IS a valid walk round the L (right 6, up 2, left 3, up 2, left 3, down 4); the item is fine.
